title: Using Adhesive Patterning to Construct 3D Paper Microfluidic Devices
protocol: Print arrays of each layer of the device onto each piece of filter paper using a solid ink printer.
Place each filter paper on a hotplate at 170 °C for 2 min.
Allow filter paper to cool to room temperature.
Deposit 4 μl of 5 mM dye in each branch of layer 3 using a micropipette.
Clamp the filter paper between the stencil and a stiff backing, such as a piece of plate glass, using binder clips.
Apply adhesive with an approximately 1.33 sec spray from about 24 cm.
Move the can of adhesive across the stencil at a medium pace.
Remove stencil and place the next layer of the device atop the freshly sprayed layer, aligning the edges of the paper.
Firmly press the two layers together.
Replace stencil and repeat the spraying process for each layer of the device.
Remove the stack of devices and place packing tape across the bottom layer.
Cut individual devices from the sheet using scissors, following the edge of the printed region.
Deposit 4 µl of 5 mM dye in each branch of layer 3 via micropipette.
Clamp the sheet of devices between the stencil and a stiff backing using binder clips.
Ensure that the stencil is flat against the paper.
Apply adhesive with an approximately 1.33 sec spray from about 24 cm, making four passes up-down-up-down.
Remove the stencil and turn the sheet over.
Replace the stencil and spray the back side of the paper.
Remove the sheet of devices after spraying both sides.
Begin folding the sheet in an accordion pleat as depicted.
Cut each device out from the sheet using scissors, following the edge of the printed region.
Place packing tape across the bottom layer.
Print crease pattern onto printer paper using a solid ink printer.
Cut the printed crease pattern to the size of the filter paper.
Place the crease pattern on a hotplate at 170 °C for 2 min.
Allow the crease pattern to cool to room temperature after removal from the hotplate.
Align the edges of the crease pattern with the edges of the paper containing channel patterns.
Attach the two pieces of paper using binder clips or another similar temporary method.
Trace the crease pattern with a blunt stylus, applying enough force that marks appear on the device sheet but not so hard that the pattern paper rips.
Begin folding the device according to the mountain and valley folds indicated by the crease pattern.
Cut out masks that limit where on the device adhesive may be applied using a razor blade.
Clamp the device between the stencil and mask and a stiff backing, ensuring the stencil is flat against the device.
Apply adhesive with an approximately 1.33 sec (a four-count at 180 bpm) spray from about 24 cm.
Remove stencil and turn the sheet over.
Replace stencil and mask and spray back side of the paper.
Immediately remove device from stencil and begin folding the device.
Once the device is completely folded, apply pressure to the adhesive containing portion until the adhesive has dried.
Construct an origami peacock according to the protocol.
Insert one end of a small paper lead (approximately 5 mm wide by 5 cm long) into the body of each peacock.
Place both peacocks in a chamber kept at a high relative humidity (>90%) to minimize evaporation.
Place each leg and lead of each peacock into a container filled with 5 mM dye.
Record wicking process with a digital camera.
